Need the MRCP report and contrast-enhanced MRI to characterize the hilar mass and its biliary involvement, plus serum total/direct bilirubin, AMA/ANA serology, and any prior RCC staging imaging to assess for metastatic disease; these are critical to verify perihilar obstruction from renal cell carcinoma metastasis and exclude PBC.
records.text:
* Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase: 257 U/L (reference: 9-32 U/L)
    * Alkaline phosphatase: 1028 U/L (reference: 106-322 U/L)
Imaging Studies:
    * Abdominal Ultrasonography
      Title: Ultrasonographic findings of hepatic parenchyma
      Description: Coarse and heterogeneous relatively hyperechoic hepatic parenchyma as a whole and an irregular isoechoic region from the hepatic hilum to the right dorsal side
    * Contrast-enhanced CT
      Title: CT findings in arterial phase
      Description: Enhancement in the liver except for the region corresponding to the isoechoic region
    * Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
      Title: MRI findings in hepatobiliary phase
      Description: Region corresponding to relatively hyperechoic hepatic parenchyma was clearly hypointense compared with hyperintensity in the region corresponding to the isoechoic region
Pathological Findings:
    * Liver Biopsy (hyperechoic parenchyma):
      - Scattered clusters of malignant cells positive for PAX8
      - Malignant cells in Glisson's capsule, occluding interlobular vein
      - Inflammatory cells infiltrated into portal canal with destroyed interlobular bile ducts
    * Liver Biopsy (isoechoic region):
      - Rare malignant cells
      - Slight inflammatory change.

records.query: Need the patient's MRCP/ERCP to directly assess perihilar biliary obstruction, along with serum total/direct bilirubin and cholestatic serology (AMA/ANA) to exclude immune-mediated cholangiopathy; additionally, clarify the renal cell carcinoma history and axitinib indication, as metastatic perihilar mass is the leading refinement.

Need the patient's MRCP or ERCP findings to directly confirm perihilar biliary obstruction, and the documented history of renal cell carcinoma with axitinib indication to substantiate metastatic etiology, as these are the core missing items for validating the leading hypothesis.

bindings.label: A 27-year-old woman presented with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes
The patient occasionally drank alcohol and was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
The patient had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, the patient's hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Physical examination showed no specific findings
Drug-induced liver injury
Chronic liver disease
Biliary/cholestatic disease
Laboratory tests show ALP 1028 U/L and GGT 257 U/L
Ultrasound shows rough uneven liver parenchyma and an irregular isoechoic area from the porta hepatis to the right dorsal side
The patient may have an immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy such as primary biliary cholangitis
The patient may have extrahepatic/perihilar biliary obstruction
Immune-mediated intrahepatic cholangiopathy (e.g., primary biliary cholangitis)
Extrahepatic/perihilar biliary obstruction
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to metastatic malignancy (e.g., renal cell carcinoma metastasis)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to benign inflammatory stricture (e.g., primary sclerosing cholangitis or IgG4-related disease)
Perihilar biliary obstruction due to choledocholithiasis/Mirizzi syndrome
Liver biopsy reveals PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with destruction of interlobular bile ducts
Immunohistochemical staining is positive for PAX8, a marker consistent with renal cell carcinoma
Contrast-enhanced CT/MRI show enhancement patterns corresponding to the hilar irregular isoechoic region
Axitinib is a targeted therapeutic agent primarily used for renal cell carcinoma
